title: Container Maintenance and Cleanup knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Container Maintenance and Cleanup”?
options: Assume one successful command proves security, persistence, and production readiness.
Change global daemon settings before establishing a baseline or reading the documentation.
Ignore the actual output and infer success from a command returning without a visible error.
Explain listing unused containers, then verify the expected behavior in a small, controlled Docker lab.
questions.answer_key: Explain listing unused containers, then verify the expected behavior in a small, controlled Docker lab.
questions.explanation: This lesson covers container maintenance and cleanup and the related syllabus points. Learners should describe the relevant concept, make a prediction, and verify it rather than rely on an untested assumption.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering container maintenance and cleanup, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to container maintenance and cleanup fails, which response is best?
options: Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For container maintenance and cleanup, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
